paragraphs: The following assessments concern management analysts' consulting and analysis work. They do not predict hiring, qualifications, authorization, or contract outcomes.

The core work of management analysts is to help management operate more efficiently through organizational studies and evaluations: collect and organize information about problems or procedures, plan work and procedure studies covering organizational change, communication, information flows, and cost analysis, interview personnel and observe on site, analyze data and develop solutions or alternative methods, document findings and recommend implementation, write manuals and train staff, review the formats, distribution, and uses of forms and reports, design records management procedures, and design area layouts and recommend purchases.

Entirely fictional task package: provide fictional department process interview records and data, including 1 current process, 1 set of key metrics, and 1 bottleneck to resolve. Within 60 minutes, write a research plan, interview and observation points, a data analysis framework, two alternative solutions, and implementation recommendations and risks. Do not use real company, client, or employee data.

Sample output and reflection: check whether you first defined the problem and scope, explained data sources and definitions, offered comparable alternatives and grounds for tradeoffs, and specified implementation and risks. Then ask whether you can remain objective amid competing stakeholder needs and deadlines, and whether you are willing to take responsibility for the evidence and consequences of recommendations.

This page covers O*NET 13-1111.00 management analysts: conducting organizational studies and evaluations, designing systems and procedures, carrying out work simplification and measurement studies, and writing operations and procedure manuals to help management operate more efficiently and effectively, including program analysts and management consultants. Work includes collecting and organizing problem information, planning work studies, interviews and on-site observation, data analysis and solutions, findings and recommendations, manuals and training, form and report reviews, and designing records management procedures and storage layouts. Work mainly takes place in offices and at client sites. This page excludes adjacent roles such as financial and investment analysts, market research analysts, project management specialists, accountants, and auditors.

entries: Inputs: problems and processes under study, interview and observation materials, operational and financial data, forms and reports, organizational and job information, external benchmarks and research, client requirements, and project scope statements.

Inspectable outputs: research plans and problem definitions, interview and observation records, data analyses and conclusions, alternative solutions and implementation recommendations, operations and procedure manuals, training materials, form and report improvement plans, records management procedures and layout recommendations, and project delivery reports.

Complete workflow: define the problem and study scope → collect materials, interview, and observe → analyze data and test hypotheses → develop alternatives and tradeoffs → produce recommendations and implementation plans → write manuals and train → follow implementation and review results.

paragraphs: Key judgments: whether problem definitions and scope are clear, data definitions and sources are reliable, alternatives are comparable and implementable, how to manage implementation resistance and risks, and whether recommendations exceed authorization or professional competence.

Environment and pace: mainly offices and client sites, mostly full time, involving prolonged reading and analysis, meetings and communication, and report writing. Deadlines and competing stakeholder needs create pressure; travel and cross-team collaboration may be required.

Research inputs: occupational identity, tasks, work activities, work context, skills and knowledge, interest code, education, and Job Zone for O*NET 13-1111.00. Pay, employment, and industry data on that page cover this occupation. These findings do not establish mainland Chinese qualifications, wages, or employment categories.

Check first: problems and objectives, study scope and authorization, data sources and definitions, stakeholders and decision chains, implementation resources and constraints, and the strength and boundaries of evidence supporting conclusions.

Work cycle: start with problem and scope definition, continue through material collection, interviews and observation, data analysis, alternatives and recommendations, manuals and training, and finish with implementation follow-up and review. Do not conclude before data definitions and authorization boundaries are confirmed or recommend rollout before implementation risks are assessed.

Boundaries with adjacent duties: this page covers only management analysts. Financial and investment analysts handle investment analysis, market research analysts handle market and marketing research, project management specialists handle project delivery, and accountants and auditors handle accounting and auditing. Professional judgments and statutory responsibilities must not be treated as interchangeable with this role.

Financial and investment analysts focus on investment opportunities and financial performance assessment. Management analysts focus on organizational, process, and operational improvements; analysis objects and decision uses differ.

Market research analysts focus on markets, consumers, and marketing effectiveness. Management analysts focus on organizational processes and operational efficiency, using similar research methods in different problem domains.

Project management specialists deliver projects within scope, schedules, and budgets. Management analysts provide research and recommendations and often assist projects but have different responsibilities.

Accountants and auditors handle accounting and auditing and take responsibility for reports. Management analysts use financial data to support process improvements without assuming accounting or auditing responsibility.
Boundaries of AI impact on management analysts

Editorial task hypothesis: distinguish traditional statistics, process mining, and knowledge retrieval from generative AI. The latter may draft consulting documents using fictional materials. Existing BCG/GPT-4 experiments support trials on specific tasks, not outcomes for all models or client projects. Original data, problem premises, causality, and solution tradeoffs require verification. Do not upload client confidential information without approval. AI Impact Score 58% is an editorial estimate. Model impact index for three equally weighted representative core tasks; not a measured share of working time or a job-loss probability. floor((75+75+25)/3+0.5)=58; fermatmind-ai-impact-v1; 2026-10-18.The three tasks, ratings and sources are listed in the FermatMind method source record on this page.

Occupational sources describe actual tasks and objects handled: problems and processes, interviews and data, forms and reports, manuals and recommendations. Tool capabilities, organizational adoption, and job outcomes are recorded separately; pay or employment data do not substitute for AI evidence.

The 2026 management consulting experiment by Dell’Acqua and colleagues, involving BCG, 758 participants, and GPT-4, found that performance may improve on tasks within the model's capabilities, while correctness may worsen on complex tasks outside them. It supports task-level trials and review, not Chinese adoption rates, effects for all models, or layoffs.

Human control points include defining problems and scope, judging data definitions and evidence strength, making solution tradeoffs amid competing stakeholder needs, taking responsibility for recommendations and consequences, and respecting authorization and professional boundaries.

Start with an offline exercise using entirely fictional process interview records and data. Record research plans, analysis frameworks, and alternative solution boundaries, without relying on unverified automated analysis to replace human judgment.

Editorial trial suggestion: a small sample draft using fictional materials only. Ordinary dedicated software differs from generative AI; widespread organizational adoption in this occupation has not been established.
Follow problem definitions, data definitions, and professional boundaries, retaining human judgment and records.

Fit signals: start with observable work behavior

To assess fit, first consider whether you can break ambiguous problems into researchable frameworks, interview patiently and analyze data objectively, make and communicate tradeoffs amid competing stakeholder needs and deadlines, take responsibility for recommendations and consequences, and keep learning industries and methods. Tools such as RIASEC can only suggest hypotheses and cannot replace real task experience.
Positive signals: structured problem decomposition, objective analysis and validation, communication that moves stakeholders forward, responsibility for conclusions, and continuous learning.

Reasons for caution: difficulty defining problems amid ambiguity and competing stakeholder needs, a tendency to tailor conclusions to demands rather than evidence, reluctance to communicate and drive progress, or inability to handle deadline pressure.

Trial activity: use entirely fictional process interview records and data to practice problem definition, analysis frameworks, alternatives, and implementation recommendations. Ask another person to review the records.

The RIASEC interest code is CIE, Conventional–Investigative–Enterprising: a preference for organizing information under procedures, research and analysis, and driving improvements. These labels describe activity preferences only and cannot determine competence or qualifications.

General personality scales such as the Big Five do not provide job evidence for this occupation and may be used only for self-reflection. Continue checking against real research and analysis, interview communication, and recommendation implementation experience.
Type tools such as MBTI and the Enneagram cannot determine competence or qualifications and may be used only for self-reflection.

Entry paths and stages of capability

O*NET's surveyed education requirements for this occupation are 57% bachelor's degrees, 24% master's degrees, and 10% some college without a degree, not legal requirements for all jobs. Job Zone4 is general group preparation information. BLS describes a bachelor's degree as typical, with some employers preferring an MBA and also considering related experience. Do not turn group training periods into uniform thresholds.

US BLS lists a bachelor's degree as typical entry education, with suitable backgrounds including business, social science, and engineering, and some employers preferring an MBA. Business is not the only path. No one-to-one Chinese qualification mapping for 13-1111.00 has been established. Check industry activities and employer requirements; refer accounting, legal, and other work requiring professional authorization to qualified personnel.

Education, professional certification, and professional practice qualifications such as accounting, law, and auditing are different statuses. Consulting certification does not automatically confer professional practice qualifications. Legally regulated professional conclusions must be issued by appropriately qualified institutions or personnel.

Entry stage: practice problem structuring, material collection and interviews, basic data analysis, and document writing under supervision. Learn industry and compliance requirements and retain process records.

Evidence to show: provide a reviewable explanation of research deliverables, including problem definition, data definitions, analytical conclusions, and alternatives, to demonstrate structured analysis and truthful documentation.

Next step: check the target employer's industry and method requirements, data and compliance constraints, decision chains, and authorization scope. Validate analysis, communication, and progress-driving skills through supervised real projects.

Moving toward greater responsibility: with experience, workers may handle end-to-end projects and client relationships, mentor new workers and develop methods, or move into industry specialization, management consulting partnership, and internal strategic management.

source_card.note: Check source scope, limitations, and statistical periods separately against original evidence. Source usage notes: O*NET 13-1111.00 Management Analysts (Summary) provides occupational identity, official description, interest code, Job Zone, skills, and knowledge for 13-1111.00. Pay and employment data on that page cover this occupation. O*NET 13-1111.00 Tasks provides tasks including collecting and organizing information, planning work studies, interviews and on-site observation, data analysis and solutions, documenting findings and recommendations, manuals and training, form and report reviews, and designing records management procedures. The task sample does not imply that every job performs all tasks. O*NET 13-1111.00 Work Context describes offices and client sites, communication and deadline pressure, and teamwork. US work context does not replace Chinese law or employer procedures. O*NET 13-1111.00 National Wages (BLS OEWS display) provides 2025 BLS OEWS median pay for this occupation. This page does not display pay percentiles. O*NET 13-1111.00 National Employment Trends provides 2024 employment and projections for growth and openings during 2024–2034. Projections do not guarantee hiring. Industries: 13-1111.00 lists Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services and Government as the main industries in 2024. Industry distribution signals employer settings, not projected growth or demand. O*NET 13-1111.00 Education and Job Preparation: Job Zone 4, most jobs require a four-year bachelor's degree and some require a master's degree, usually with several years of related work or vocational training. The education distribution does not establish a mandatory requirement for every employer. National Certifications: 13-1111.00 is the US national certification lookup provided by O*NET. Certification and training do not establish professional practice qualifications or employer hiring requirements. Generative AI and Jobs (ILO Working Paper 140, 2025) assesses occupational exposure to generative AI at the task level. The exposure index does not equal adoption rates, job outcomes, or hiring probabilities. Average Annual Wages of Employees in Urban Units in 2025 provides average annual wages by industry category for urban nonprivate and private units, including leasing and business services. Industry averages are not occupational medians and exclude individual businesses and freelancers. Enterprise Remuneration Survey Information (2024) from the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security is a pay lookup organized by occupation / position. It covers urban enterprises, excluding government agencies and public institutions; this page did not obtain an entry precisely matching this occupation. The FermatMind Task Impact Scale for Management Analysts organizes tasks that tools may assist and human control points for task-level AI and fit discussion. The editorial scale is not evidence of adoption rates, layoffs, regulations, or credentials.
